column1: # classdesc+0xF4 per class - the value the four member accessors SUBTRACT from a recorded
# member offset before adding it to the instance pointer (0063C4A0, 0063D300, 0063AD90,
# +0xF4 is NOT a constant. 0063E410 zeroes it and then accumulates it around the parent
# chain - `add dword [rdx+0xF4], [rax+0xF0]`, following +0x78, stopping at the root
# descriptor 02CF8270. +0xF0 is arg7 of the descriptor constructor; across all calls to
# 00632D80/00632C90, 298 pass 0, 16 pass 8, one passes 1, one passes -2, 69 pass r15d.
# UNRESOLVED means a register argument somewhere in that chain, NOT zero. Assuming zero is
# precisely the error this table exists to correct.
# RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (OPUS). +0xF4 == +0xF8 for all 153 classes where both resolve (0
# differences), so the four accessors (which subtract +0xF4) and the per-instance initialiser
# 0063C910 (which subtracts +0xF8) resolve a runtime object pointer to the SAME layout base.
# The recorded offsets are measured from THAT base and need no adjustment: all 27 classes with
# 0x8 have every offset inside [0, instanceSize), and PNode has a member at +0x0, which could
# not be true if the offsets were object-pointer-relative and needed 8 subtracted.
# THE ONE CONSEQUENCE FOR A RECONSTRUCTION: for the 27 classes below with 0x8, a runtime object
# pointer is layoutBase + 8, so a live pointer converts to a field address as
# (pointer - 8) + offset. For the other 126 the two are the same.
